newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 9-mth farm sector growth seen at 4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 9-mth farm sector growth seen at 4 pct.

text.p: The Philippine agriculture sector is expected to surpass its 1996 growth forecast of four percent, but the country may have to export more corn in 1997 to meet rising demand, Agriculture Minister Salvador Escudero said.
"We are confident that the agriculture sector grew beyond four percent in the first nine months of the year," Escudero said on Saturday.
He added he expected the sector's recovery to be sustained for the rest of the year largely due to a rise in rice output.

Philippine agriculture, which economists have described as the "Achilles heel" of the country's overall economic growth, grew by just 0.9 percent in 1995 due to a dry spell that led to rice shortages.
Overall gross national product growth was 5.7 percent.
Agriculture officials said better rice harvests this year would offset slowdowns in other agricultural products, such as coconuts.
Escudero told reporters he expected unmilled rice production to grow 9.3 percent this year to 11.52 million tonnes from the year-ago 10.54 million.
"The expected increase in the total output is attributed to the combined effect of a 5.4 percent expansion in area harvested and yield improvement of 3.9 percent," Escudero said.
Corn production was expected to increase by 0.73 percent to 4.16 million tonnes this year from 4.13 million a year ago due to a 1.4 percent increase in total acreage.
Escudero said corn production dropped by 15.2 percent in the third quarter this year from the year-ago level due to pest infestations and weather problems.
Corn output in the fourth quarter was also expected to drop by six percent compared to the third quarter due to a delayed harvest and replantings in northern Luzon, he added.
"Corn importation is inevitable next year, but we have to study figures on demand between December this year and February next year," Escudero said.
The Department of Agriculture earlier projected local corn demand of 5.5 million tonnes in 1996.
"Corn shortfall this year is between 400,000 tonnes to 1.2 million, depending on the growth of the livestock sector," Escudero said.

Since the start of the year, the Philippines has imported 400,000 tonnes of corn, including 150,000 tonnes of yellow corn number two bought by the National Food Authority (NFA) from the United States last month at an average $161.10 C&F per tonne.

Livestock farmers have asked the NFA to import an additional 250,000 tonnes due to prospects of low corn supply in the first quarter of 1997. The private sector usually asks the NFA to import corn on its behalf to take advantage of low tariffs.
Escudero said the government will have to study the impact of the 150,000 tonnes of corn on the local market before deciding on the proposal of livestock farmers.
Manila grains traders have said they do not expect additional rice imports for the rest of the year.
The Philippines has so far imported 846,000 tonnes of rice in the year to August.

The country's rice inventory reached 1.35 million tonnes as of October 1 this year, 25 percent higher compared to the year-ago level. "This stock inventory is sufficient to meet the 63-day requirement of the country," the department said.
The country's corn stock as of October 1 dropped 7.7 percent to 418,100 tonnes from the year-ago level, Escudero added.
Unmilled rice output in the first quarter of 1997 was expected to increase by 6.1 percent to 3.68 million tonnes compared to the same period last year based on planting intentions by farmers.
Corn output in the same period was expected to rise by 8.2 percent to 1.13 million tonnes from the year-ago production, Escudero said.
